subject: Potential Data Exposure — evidence staging & notification cadence
messages:
From: Alice Jeong <alice.jeong@greenleafhealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: CISO Greenleaf <ciso@greenleafhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unusual external access to GLH customer bucket — initial ask

Hi Logan,

We found multiple unusual GET requests to the GLH model-artifacts S3 prefix between 02:30–03:10 UTC this morning; the requests originated from IP ranges we don't recognize. We ran a quick scan and attached the initial-scan-output.jsonl for your visibility.

Can Redwood confirm whether any customer payloads or model prompt data were returned to an external host? Greenleaf has regulatory obligations here (potential HIPAA-sensitive metadata). We need to preserve evidence and understand the notification cadence you can commit to if this escalates.

Requested from Redwood:
- Immediate preservation of access logs and any relevant KV cache snapshots
- A 72-hour initial assessment window to determine scope
- Point of contact for forensic handoff and a list of what Redwood can provide for a formal evidence package

We're trying to avoid premature escalation while meeting our internal reporting timelines. Appreciate a clear mutual action plan and the earliest ETA for an assessment.

Thanks,
Alice Jeong
Director, Platform Security
Greenleaf Health

Attachment: initial-scan-output.jsonl (3.2 MB)
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jeong <alice.jeong@greenleafhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual external access to GLH customer bucket — initial ask

Alice — thanks for the heads up and the scan output. We're treating this with high priority. Preliminary notes and proposed mutual action plan below.

Mutual action plan (high level):
1) Evidence preservation (immediate) — Redwood will snapshot S3 access logs, load-balancer logs, model-gateway request traces, and any active KV cache state for GLH for the 24-hour window you flagged. We will not rotate or purge related logs until we've handed them to Greenleaf or a designated forensics partner.
2) 72-hour triage — Redwood's infra/security team (Ben) + product ops (me) will run an initial scope review in 72 hours and report whether there is confirmed data exfiltration or false positives.
3) Forensic handoff (if warranted) — if triage indicates potential exposure, we will produce a forensics bundle (logs, SHA256 manifest, access-control snapshots, and ingestion metadata) and coordinate a joint transfer to your chosen vendor. Expected handoff target: 7 calendar days from confirmation.
4) Notification cadence — Redwood can commit to an initial summary within 72 hours, then daily status updates until the scope is closed. Formal breach notification commitments (timing & regulatory language) will follow the DPA clauses; we'll align on exact wording if we confirm exposure.

What Redwood needs from Greenleaf immediately:
- Confirmation of the set of resource identifiers you consider in-scope (bucket prefixes, model ids)
- Confirmation of forensics vendor (if you already have one) or permission for Redwood to propose Cybersafe Forensics
- Point-of-contact for legal/regulatory (for DocuSign authorization if cross-border transfer is required)

I've attached a short forensics-instructions.pdf that outlines how we'll collect and package artifacts. Ben — can you start the evidence preservation run and open a secure transfer bucket (read-only for GLH + upload for forensics)? Marissa — can you review the notification cadence and prepare a draft of the DPA-triggered notification wording?

I'll follow up in Slack with the IR channel.

Best,
Logan Wright
Site Reliability & Customer Ops
Redwood Inference

Marissa here — quick additions from a contractual perspective:
- Subprocessors: Please confirm whether GLH considers Redwood's vector index vendor (VectorBox) and our CDN provider in-scope for the evidence bundle. If so, we'll route requests to their compliance contacts and include their logs if available.
- Cross-border transfer: if the evidence contains EU/UK/other personal data, we'll need an executed Data Processing Addendum (DPA) section/authorization permitting Redwood to transfer logs to the forensics vendor and, if necessary, to a cross-border forensics lab. I attached an evidence-request-template.docx with the typical fields we capture for DPA sign-off.
- SOC 2 artifacts: Cybersafe requested the latest SOC 2 status and the control mapping for log retention windows; I'll coordinate an export.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Unusual external access to GLH customer bucket — initial ask

Thanks everyone — this plan is workable. Greenleaf confirms the following in-scope identifiers: s3://glh-prod/model-artifacts/, model-id: glh-clinical-v2, and the associated ingestion prefixes. We will engage Cybersafe as our forensics vendor and have included them on this thread.

A few operational notes:
- We need a read-only forensics bucket and a transfer manifest with checksums.
- If Redwood's collection includes any patient-identifiable fields, Greenleaf will require that the transfer be executed under an authorized DPA addendum (we can sign via DocuSign).
- Please kick off the preservation run now; we'll expect the 72-hour summary by Friday 09:00 PT.

Marissa — I reviewed the evidence-request-template and will fill the sections related to regulatory timelines. Please send the DocuSign link for the transfer authorization when ready.

Appreciate the quick triage.

— Alice
